title: One missing quote breaks the catalog
scenario: One disconnected lamp Shipping path fails the whole delivery catalog, hiding healthy chair and desk results. Availability still works because it does not use Shipping.
why: A fast failure can break the catalog without filling workers. An unavailable lamp quote should preserve the other products without inventing delivery data.
reproduce: Disconnect Shipping in Network Faults. Compare “Refresh all availability” and “Preview all deliveries”.
ready: Clear all faults and restore default settings. Start the stack with the launcher. Keep background traffic unchanged; compare fresh 60–90-second windows and changes in rejected requests. Use Storefront for customer results and Grafana for workers, queue, rejections and dependency circuits.
assignment: Can you contain the outage to one unavailable lamp quote?

tasks.title: Compare both healthy catalog views
tasks.instruction: Refresh availability and preview deliveries. Record all products, timings and queue state. Set an abort condition and predict which view Shipping affects.

tasks.title: Disconnect only lamp Shipping
tasks.instruction: Disconnect Shipping and repeat both views. Record catalog failure, working availability and Shipping errors. Check whether the queue actually fills.

tasks.title: Identify the coupling
tasks.instruction: Check “Customer request rate”, “Dependency outcomes” and workers. Explain why one missing quote hides healthy products, and how this differs from Challenge 1.

tasks.title: Allow an honest partial catalog
tasks.instruction: Reconnect Shipping. Apply Challenge 2 settings: Shipping fallback and a 5-second breaker. Keep the 3000 ms timeout for this immediate failure.

tasks.title: Repeat and measure the smaller impact
tasks.instruction: Disconnect Shipping again. Compare catalog status, fallback activity and live chair/desk quotes; only the lamp quote should be unavailable. Clear faults, restore defaults, and allow in-flight requests and a 5-second cooldown to finish. Verify live stock and delivery for all products, then submit your measurements.

done: You compared both complete-catalog views before, during and after mitigation of the same outage.
You showed healthy chair/desk delivery information surviving while only the lamp quote remained unavailable.
You explained aggregate error propagation without assuming a fast failure saturates workers, then restored all paths and defaults.
solution: A missing lamp quote fails /api/catalog?preview=true. Availability works without Shipping.
Shipping fallback returns an unavailable lamp quote, preserving lamp stock and live chair/desk data without inventing a price or date.
The breaker pauses failed lamp Shipping calls for 5 seconds before a probe. Fast failures may leave the queue empty.
Reconnect, restore defaults and verify live data for all products. Compare equal observation windows.

fields.label: Healthy baseline and metric
fields.prompt: Record your baseline. Include all the data you identify as relevant from Grafana into your notes. Watch healthy availability and delivery carefully.

fields.label: Hypothesis, blast radius, and abort condition
fields.prompt: What could be the impact of an unavailable shipping service? Which functions will fail?

fields.label: Outage evidence
fields.prompt: Introduce the fault by deactivating the shipping service. Investigate availability and deliveries on the Storefront. Include all products and catalog time/status; record queue size and new rejections from Grafana over the same window.

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: Why allow an unavailable quote? Explain timeout, breaker and fallback separately.

fields.label: Same-outage validation
fields.prompt: Record results under the same outage. Include all products and catalog time/status; record queue size and new rejections from Grafana over the same window.

fields.label: Blast-radius conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: Did the impact shrink? What is still missing? Confirm cleanup.

mitigationHelp.description: Shipping fallback preserves the catalog with an unavailable lamp quote; the breaker pauses failed calls for 5 seconds.
mitigationHelp.instruction: Use Challenge 2 settings. A slow Shipping fault also needs a shorter timeout.
